The interior of the cab has a faceplate with the serial numbers of the maintenance, technical, and parts manuals. The maintenance manual details.... well, maintenance. The technical manual tells you how to take everything apart to the point that you could have a pile of spare parts if you want and then put it back together. The parts manual lists all of the part numbers for everything on the truck and everything used on the truck (like GAA grease - General Automotive and Artillery). The tech manual is 1209 pages. I had that one printed. Cost something like $200 and the print shop loved me enough to give me a volume discount. Aside from that, you can go to youtube where there a LOT of videos on maintenance and modifications. You can also go to forums like https://www.steelsoldiers.com/ where owners talk about their rigs, maintenance, ask questions, etc. For example, GAA grease costs $600ish for 5 gallons. There's a modern replacement that is much cheaper and exceeds milspec... Mobile One Synthetic and it's $95.90 for 5 gallons assuming you get the expensive 12 ounce grease gun tubes. As far as anything you can't do yourself, there are truck garages which cater exclusively to semis and similar rigs and some will do road calls. The road calls are more expensive because there's a road call fee and higher labor costs.

There are other things you learn as you go. For example, the tires on it now are milspec ND 9x20 tires and they run $300ish each. Ten tires = $3000 for a new set. You can get them cheaper if you're lucky. But ND tires (non-directional) are only so no one can tell which way you're going by looking at your vehicle's tracks. Mud tires get better traction and are cheaper. So, a lot of it is learned "as you go" and "trial and error".
